conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Pointillism
style.description: A big stretched canvas in a bright warm studio, painted only with small round dabs of pure, unmixed paint from a ten-hue palette (no browns, greys or black). Each dab has a little raised relief, a darker rim and a wet highlight; cream canvas weave shows between them. A planner (dots.js) builds an original sunlit scene from gradients and shapes, scatters ~10,000 dots on a jittered grid and gives each one a pure palette colour by a seeded rule so the local average matches the scene: mostly the two nearest pure hues in proportion, plus a share of the complementary hue in shadows. Dots pop on region by region; two round brushes dab on their own in close-up; a display-space defocus (the squint) melts the dots into the colours the eye mixes.
motion: A dab pops from nothing to full size with a small overshoot when a brush touches or when its region's flood front reaches it; it never moves again.
Regions fill one after another as ragged fronts spreading from an origin (water from the first dabs, the sky from the horizon, the tree up its trunk).
Brushes dab on their own: descend along their axis, squash, lift, hop to the next spot.
The squint is a display-space gaussian blur whose radius is a function of t; the dots melt into the colours the eye mixes and sharpen again.

notes.mechanism: dots.js: an original lake scene from gradients and shapes; 132 x 76 jittered, row-offset grid of dabs; each dab one pure palette colour from the best pair of allowed hues for the local scene colour (display sRGB), plus complementary dots in shadow; regions flood as ragged fronts; the first 8 dabs are placed by two brushes.
